note: Physical sky after Hillaire 2020 (docs/06). Planet radii are fixed at 6360 km and 6460 km in lib-atmosphere.wgsl and atmosphere-cpu.js. Coefficients are per km, heights in km unless the name says m. Stars and the Milky Way are the one art-directed term: their brightness is set in EV above the night exposure floor (EV100 -1, docs/05), not in physical units.

orbit.note: tilt 21 gives the 9.5 h midwinter and 14.5 h midsummer days doc 06 asks for; startHour sets a new world's first hour

albedo.note: relative albedo; the full disk averages about 1 so it integrates to illuminanceFull

groundAerosol.note: Diorama haze: a local Mie layer hugging the ground. scatteringPerKm is at sea level for density 1; slightly bluer at short wavelengths (Angstrom exponent about 1.3).

probe.note: Sky probe cube for reflections (docs/06, 07): face size per tier in quality-tiers.json skyProbeSize, full mip chain, mip m = perceptual roughness m / (mips - 1). prefilterSamples is the GGX sample count per texel for each blurred mip (more is smoother and slower; 16 to 64). horizonBlendDeg is how far below the horizon the sky fades into the ground hemisphere, so reflections show no seam.

starlight.note: Art-directed, like the stars: a faint cool glow added to the airglow shell, standing in for starlight, zodiacal light and the eye's dark adaptation. Physically a moonless sky is about 8 EV darker than a full-moon one; with this it is about 4 EV darker, so moonless nights keep readable shapes (docs/05 night key). Ignored by day: it is a millionth of daylight.

overcast.note: cloud blends the sky toward a gray CIE overcast dome whose horizontal illuminance is the clear sky plus sunToDome of the direct sun
